html:
The Free County of Burgundy, or Franche-Comté, was a county in what is now eastern France, between Burgundy and Switzerland, with Besançon and Dole as its main towns. It is on the map for 1650 and 1700.

It lay inside the Holy Roman Empire, not France. Through the Dukes of Burgundy it passed to the Habsburgs in the late 1400s and then to the kings of Spain, who ruled it from far away and let it keep wide freedoms.

Louis XIV wanted it. He overran it in 1668 but gave it back that year. In 1674 he conquered it again, and the Treaties of Nijmegen in 1678 made it French for good. His engineer Vauban rebuilt the citadel of Besançon. By the 1700 map it is a province of France.
